BACONC P' LIANAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO s. 2021 17 HON. GLENN C. BERCEDE Vice Mayor Mandaue City, Cebu Dear Hon. Bercede: This has reference to the letter received by the Department last 5 September 2024 pertaining to the request for clarification on matters outlined in the Memorandum dated 24 August 2024 issued by the DILG Region VII in reference to the Decision in the Ombudsman in the case of Sereno Gabayan Monsanto, et.al vs. Jonas C. Cortes, et. The following points were raised, to wit: (I) The Ombudsman Decision is silent or lacks directives on how it should be implemented or enforced. It did not categorically direct the DILG to carry out the implementation; and (2) There is no separate order directing the incumbent Mayor to vacate his seat in the office. In addition, mere service of the Decision upon Mayor Cortes does not ipso facto result in a vacancy of his office, absent the overt act of the DILG in implementing the said Decision. We shall discuss the following points together. We affirm that the dispositive portion of the Ombudsman Decision did not clearly state that the Department is directed to implement it against Hon. Jonas C. Cortes. In the interest of due diligence and to not cause further delay in public service, the regional office was directed to verify the status of its implementation and verify if such vacancy existedl. Through the Mandaue City Public Information Office (PIO), Official Facebook page, it was verified that the aforementioned Decision was served upon Mayor Cortes on 21 August 2024. In addition, local media outlets confirmed receipt of the Ombudsman Decision on the same date. The authority of the Department to implement the Ombudsman Decision upon receipt thereof is pursuant to Section 7, Rule Ill of [Ombudsman Rules of Procedure] in relation to Memorandum Circular No. I, Series of 2006 dated II April 2006. Hence, in order that the foregoing rule may be strictly observed, all concerned are enjoined to implement all Ombudsman decisions, orders or resolutions in administrative Central Office Memorandum dated 24 August 2024 to the Regional Director "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO. (02) 8876 3454

disciplinary cases, immediately upon receipt thereof by their respective offices2. Worth noting is that not all decisions of the Ombudsman are implemented by the Department. The Ombudsman can implement their own decisions which is what happened in the instant case. As already enunciated by the high court in a long line of cases and has been settled with finality, decisions of the Ombudsman in disciplinary cases are immediately executory and cannot be stayed by the filing of an appeal or the issuance of an injunctive writ3. Furthermore, jurisprudence provides that an Ombudsman's dismissal order is immediately executory and, once executed, the public officer ceases to have title for the time being. Hence, it should be considered as an interruption of his term4. Further, the Court expounded as follows: Section 7, Rule III of the Rules of Procedure of the Office of the Ombudsman, as amended by Administrative Order No. 17 dated September 15, 2003, provides: SEC. 7. Finality and execution of decision. - Where the respondent is absolved of the charge, and in case of conviction where the penalty imposed is public censure or reprimand, suspension of not more than one month, or a fine equivalent to one month salary, the decision shall be final, executory and unappealable. In all other cases, the decision may be appealed to the Court of Appeals on a verified petition for review under the requirements and conditions set forth in Rule 43 of the Rules of Court, within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the written Notice of the Decision or Order denying the motion for reconsideration. A decision of the Office of the Ombudsman in administrative cases shall be executed as a matter of course. The Office of the Ombudsman shall ensure that the decision shall be strictly enforced and properly implemented. The refusal or failure by any officer without just cause to comply with an order of the Office of the Ombudsman to remove, suspend, demote, fine, or censure shall be a ground for disciplinary action against such officer. x x x. The Ombudsman's decision imposing the penalty of suspension for one year is immediately executory pending appeal. It cannot be stayed by the mere filing of an appeal to the CA. This rule is similar to that provided under Section 47 of the Uniform Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service5 Based on the foregoing, it is clear that decisions of the Ombudsman are immediately executory and once this has been properly implemented and executed, the public officer ceases to have title for the time being, in which case a vacancy in the position MC No. 1, series of 2006. No. 246679, March 02, 2021. s OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN. PETITIONER, VS. ELMER M. PACURIBOT, RESPONDENT, G.R. NO. 193336, September 26, 2018. Page 2 of 3

is present. Considering that a temporary vacancy existed, the DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21 takes effect. In which case the next ranking official assumes the position while the cause of vacancy exists. Hence, we are of the considered view that the Vice Mayor of Mandaue, Cebu as the next ranking official, has by operation of law, the authority to assume the position of the Acting Mayor of Mandaue, Cebu. While this opinion was pending review and approval, this Department received on 04 October 2024 a copy of the Ombudsman Decision dated September 26, 2024 in OMB- V-A-MAR-23-0037 ENTITLED: "INES CORBO NECESARIO JULITA O. NARTE VS. JONAS CABUNGAL CORTES" wherein the respondent was meted a penalty of dismissal from service. We note that this case is different from the Ombudsman decision upon which your queries were based, however, it involves the same respondent. Nonetheless, we render this opinion for academic discussion purposes with emphasis that this is without prejudice to any contrary opinion that may be issued by competent authorities and/or the courts. This is likewise without prejudice to any developments that may be brought about by any pending legal remedies which may have been considered by the parties to the abovementioned cases. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: Und OU co AN VICTOR R.
